title: Session Resume Overlay
summary: Recover bounded agent task state against a verified published snapshot and the observed worktree without turning session assertions into project authority.

commands.checkpoint: checkpoint --input FILE|- --task-id ID --thread-id ID [--observed-at UNIX_SECONDS] [--jobs N] [--require-current]
commands.resume: resume --checkpoint FILE --task-id ID --thread-id ID [--task TEXT] [--observed-at UNIX_SECONDS] [--trusted-producer ID] [--jobs N] [--require-current]
commands.output: checkpoint emits one canonical compact shin.session-checkpoint.v1 document on stdout. The host persists it atomically outside the consumer. resume emits shin.session-resume.v1 on stdout.

draft.taskRequest: Existing shin.task-request.v1 with explicit reviewed evidence requirements. Session limits narrow its existing ceilings; no requirements are inferred from prose.
draft.blocked: Only kind=blocked requires blocker_kind: vpn, credentials, user, or external-state.
draft.nextActions: Ordered objects containing id and text only. They are session-proposed and require review. Arbitrary argv is not an input field.
draft.receipts: At most 32 shin.execution-receipt.v1 objects, with unique ids; assertion receipt_ids must resolve within this array.
draft.vcs: Null or {branch, commit}. Commit is a full 40- or 64-character lowercase hex object id. Metadata is session-asserted; Core does not invoke Git.
draft.ttlSeconds: Required integer in 1..604800. A host may choose 86400 for normal session state. Runtime receipts carry independent shorter TTLs.

checkpoint.binding: Canonical physical project root, profile id, profile_config_hash, opaque task_id, and opaque thread_id. Root plus profile defines project identity; task and thread prevent accidental cross-session reuse. No Git repository is required.
checkpoint.baseline: Verified snapshot_id, observed worktree_id, index_current, and observation_complete. worktree_id covers profile-owned inputs, not every file in the repository.
checkpoint.trackedSources: Sorted union of changed_paths, assertion paths, and prior Pack verification paths. Each row has path, observation, content_hash, and bytes. observation is observed, missing, or unobserved. Only profile-selected hashed source bytes count as observed; outside-profile or skipped inputs never become evidence.
checkpoint.packBaseline: Null when profile metadata prevents meaningful retrieval; otherwise receipt_id, request_fingerprint, evidence_set_fingerprint, and ordered evidence_ids. Full evidence text and chat history are not retained.
checkpoint.dirtyCapture: Without --require-current, capture is allowed while the worktree is dirty. Its prior Pack identity refers to the published snapshot; tracked file hashes refer to capture-time worktree. These two baselines remain separate.
checkpoint.identity: checkpoint_id is FNV-1a-64 of compact sorted-key JSON before adding checkpoint_id. It detects accidental drift and is not authentication.

resume.bindingMismatch: Different root, profile, task_id, or thread_id returns status=mismatched, exit 1, and no saved state or continuation Pack. Profile config drift remains inspectable within the same profile.
resume.time: captured_at and observed_at are Unix seconds. Without --observed-at Core reads system_clock after blocking input/index access, Pack retrieval, and worktree recheck, immediately before freshness assessment, and labels clock_source. Explicit time makes identical inputs deterministic. now < captured_at is future; now - captured_at >= ttl_seconds is expired.
resume.axes: checkpoint_age is current/expired/future. alignment is aligned/drifted. index_current and observation_complete are independent. status summarizes age before alignment; it does not replace the individual fields.
resume.checkpointDrift: Exact comparison of the bounded tracked source hashes against current observations. complete_historical_diff is always false. A changed whole-worktree fingerprint with no changed tracked path still requires review; Core cannot reconstruct missing historical inventory.
resume.publishedDrift: The same profile-owned comparison used by worktree-diff, with 32 details and exact omission counts, against the currently pinned published snapshot.
resume.assertions: Every saved assertion stays session-asserted and claim_verified=false. references_current means referenced bytes are unchanged; it does not prove that the bytes entail the text. receipts_current requires all named receipts to be explicitly trusted, current, correctly scoped, and passed.
resume.continuationPack: Generated only when snapshot/profile/worktree content is exactly current and source observation is complete. After input hashes match, the existing exact generated-output comparison independently verifies canonical publication, preserving normal --require-current semantics. Reuses Agent Context Pack compact projection with the saved explicit request; verification paths, completion, budgets, and provenance retain their existing semantics.
resume.currentTask: Optional --task labels the host current intent. Different wording sets task_wording_changed and disables continuation_ready. It never silently rewrites the saved objective or evidence requirements.
resume.readiness: continuation_ready requires a current index, current checkpoint age, complete Pack, no declared blocker, and unchanged task wording. review_required remains independent and may be true when drift was detected. This is task recovery readiness, not a replacement for adopted-project ready/validate gates.
resume.actions: Ordered Core policy actions precede saved session-proposed actions. A stale index includes non-executing next_command.argv for explicit build. No shell, next action, gate, receipt, or business operation is executed.
resume.exit: Successful assessment exits 0. --require-current exits 1 with the full resume envelope when the index is stale or incomplete. Expired state and declared blockers remain inspectable with continuation_ready=false. Invalid input, mismatched binding, or unavailable/corrupt snapshot fail closed.

inputSafety: Unknown fields, duplicate JSON keys, invalid enums/types, numeric overflow, path traversal, control characters in session strings, and built-in secret-like patterns are rejected. Keys, values, and session CLI text are checked; source suppressions such as gitleaks:allow have no effect on session input. Parser errors omit input excerpts. Files must be regular non-symlink files resolving outside the consumer; stdin is accepted only for drafts. This heuristic scanner is not proof that arbitrary free text is secret-free; the host must omit credentials and transcripts.
concurrency: One RetrievalSession pins the published snapshot with a shared lock. Worktree inventories and metadata are rechecked after hashing and again before output. Source state is an observation, not a lock on concurrent external writers.

hostIntegration.storage: Host-owned external state directory keyed by canonical project/worktree and task/thread. Persist stdout through temporary file plus rename, with restrictive local permissions. Save only successful checkpoint output. Do not put session files in generated KB or consumer docs.
hostIntegration.resume: Host or operator includes the checkpoint path and binding in bounded handoff state, invokes resume after recovery, and delivers its envelope to the agent. Skills document manual invocation; automatic compaction-triggered persistence and host hooks are outside this host-neutral contract and are not proposed here.
hostIntegration.handoff: A different receiving task/thread cannot consume the old checkpoint as current. Review the old state and create a new draft bound to the receiving task. No automatic rebind flag exists.

verification.appleLeaks: tests/run_leaks.sh includes checkpoint and resume child-process probes
